deep.reconstruction:
Setting: E and F are Hilbert spaces. The next page uses polar decomposition v = U|v|, which confirms this. N is a symmetric norming function on R^(N), the finitely supported sequences; Grothendieck calls these 'normes de Schatten'. ℓ^N is the maximal sequence space and ℓ_N is the closure of finite sequences in it. N' (later written N°) is the dual norming function.

For a compact u: E→F let ρ_i(u) be its singular values (s-numbers). This is the Schmidt decomposition u = Σ ρ_i ē_i⊗f_i with (e_i), (f_i) orthonormal. L^N(E,F) is the space of u with (ρ_i(u)) ∈ ℓ^N, and N(u) = N((ρ_i(u))), computed as a limit or sup over truncations.

The page does the following.
(1) It shows u ↦ N(u) is a norm. The triangle inequality comes from formula (9 bis), presumably the Ky Fan majorization of singular values of u+v by those of u and v, together with monotonicity of N under weak majorization. Homogeneity and definiteness are immediate.
(2) Margin (12)-(13): two-sided ideal property, N(su) ≤ ‖s‖N(u) and N(us) ≤ ‖s‖N(u); probably also N(u*) = N(u).
(3) L_N(E,F) is defined as the set of u with (ρ_i(u)) ∈ ℓ_N. It is the closure of the finite-rank operators E'⊗F in L^N(E,F). Proof: the Schmidt tail satisfies N(Σ_{i>n} ρ_i ē_i⊗f_i) = N(0,…,0,ρ_{n+1},…) → 0, because the shift-truncations π_n tend to 0 on ℓ_N.
(4) A crossed-out passage states the duality (L_N(E,F))' = L^{N'}(F,E) via the trace pairing. The model case is N_1, where trace class has dual L(F,E) = L^{N_∞}. It also states the Hölder estimate ‖vu‖_1 ≤ N(u)N'(v). This is redone properly on the next page, with a proof via v ≥ 0, a diagonal reduction, and a projector of infinite rank.
(5) General Hölder inequality for operator ideals: suppose N, N', N'' are symmetric norming functions with N(xy) ≤ N'(x)N''(y) for sequences. The inequality then extends to ℓ^{N'}·ℓ^{N''}. For u ∈ L^{N'}(E,F) and v ∈ L^{N''}(F,G) one gets vu ∈ L^N(E,G) with N(vu) ≤ N'(u)N''(v), formula (16).

Overall this is the basic theory of symmetrically normed ideals of operators on Hilbert space: maximal and separable ideals, density of finite rank, trace duality, and Hölder inequalities. It serves Grothendieck's 1953 study of tensor norms and operator classes.
errors: Gap in (16): passing from the sequence inequality N(xy) ≤ N'(x)N''(y) to operators needs the singular-value inequality s(vu) ≺_w s(u)s(v). This follows from Horn's log-majorization, which implies weak majorization. It also needs monotonicity of N under weak majorization. The visible page only says 'la formule … pour x∈ℓ^{N'}, y∈ℓ^{N''}' without stating this step; it may have been in earlier formulas such as (9 bis).

The duality (L_N)' = L^{N'} was struck out here, presumably because the proof was incomplete. It is re-proved on the next page. The distinction L_N ≠ L^N (e.g. N_∞: compacts versus all bounded operators) is handled correctly, as on the previous page for sequences.

ideas.what: Norm ideals L^N (maximal) and L_N (separable part, closure of finite rank) of Hilbert-space operators defined by a symmetric norming function applied to singular values
ideas.modern_name: Symmetrically normed operator ideals S_Φ and S_Φ^(0)
ideas.usually_credited_to: von Neumann (1937, symmetric gauge functions), Schatten (1946/1950, 1960 book), Gohberg–Krein (1965)
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in Grothendieck's 1955 Memoir (Produits tensoriels topologiques) in the discussion of Hilbert-space tensor norms; unsure.

ideas.what: Triangle inequality for N(u) via majorization of singular values of a sum
ideas.modern_name: Ky Fan majorization / Ky Fan dominance
Duality of symmetrically normed ideals (S_Φ^(0))* = S_{Φ*}

ideas.what: Hölder inequality N(vu) ≤ N'(u)N''(v) whenever the norming functions satisfy the sequence Hölder relation
ideas.modern_name: Hölder inequality for symmetric norm ideals / product of operator ideals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gohberg–Krein; Schatten; later Pietsch (operator ideal products)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean early (1953) development of symmetrically normed ideals, including trace duality and general Hölder inequalities. Historically it is interesting as Grothendieck's private parallel to Schatten and an anticipation of Gohberg–Krein. However, all of it is standard theory, and Schatten had much of it by 1950.
transcription_corrections: The 'f_i' in '(f_i(u)) ∈ ℓ_N' and in 'Σ f_i ē_i⊗f_i' should read ρ_i, the singular values: u = Σ ρ_i ē_i⊗f_i (Schmidt decomposition). This is consistent with 'v = Σ ρ_i e_i⊗e_i' on the next page.
'N(‖f_i;u+v‖…)' is likely N((ρ_i(u+v))_{i≤n}), i.e. N evaluated on truncated singular-value sequences.
Margin likely reads: N(u*) = N(u) [or N(λu)=|λ|N(u)], N(su) ≤ ‖s‖N(u), N(us) ≤ ‖s‖N(u) (13), and (14) relating L^N to L(E,F) / L_N when N = N° or N = N_∞.
Crossed passage: 'le dual de L_{N_1}(E,F) = L^1(E,F) [est] L(F,E)'.
